finding: Specified finite studies document both benefits and failures of pivot ordering, simplification, feedback and retained boundary relations; a one-step no-growth certificate is conditional.
limitations: No general 3-SAT algorithm, P-versus-NP result or universal speedup is established.
Original challenge screenshots were not recovered; JH is credited for the originating challenge, not the later mathematical implementation.
Some checks are same-author; recorded proxy units do not measure complete elapsed-time or full cost.
Selected programs and data are source inspection material and may not be a standalone replay package.
Five supplied editorial files differ from the accompanying manifest; this article is a separately hashed derivative of the actually received text.
method: Historical MATH research reports on resolution, subsumption, adaptive feedback, conditional safe elimination and boundary-relation representations; retain existing finite tests and checks.
open_questions: When can reusable boundary relationships be found and maintained at a net benefit under a fair complete-cost comparison?
Can pressure detection avoid both expensive late triggers and unnecessary cleanup?
